D_throughput.S376_decision_rule: Peak capacity supports authorization readiness but does not prove sustainability. The expansion decision should not hinge on sustainability proof — that's a post-authorization monitoring metric.

The S376 decision explicitly said sustainability proof should NOT block authorization, making this a post-authorization monitoring metric rather than a blocker. However, the current state (zero authoring between S376 and S379) means the throughput model has shown PEAK but not STEADY-STATE operation.

But full multi-week sustainability proof (3 consecutive weeks) requires calendar time — not resolvable in 1-2 sessions. A strong 2-session sprint (e.g., 40-60 items, 0 defects) would substantially improve confidence but not constitute PROOF of sustainability.
D_throughput.recommendation: Run a 2-session sustained-authoring sprint in S380-S381 (target: 30-40 items with Evaluate items prioritized). Track defect rate, session duration, and items/session. This proves the model is replicable even if not yet 'proven sustainable.'
